skills.name: Common application software 2: presentations and databases

note.text:
• Presentation software (e.g. Microsoft PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress): slides with text, pictures, charts, animations and transitions, for talks and lessons. Good slides: few words, large clear text, relevant images.
• Database management software (e.g. Microsoft Access): stores large amounts of organised data so it can be searched, sorted and reported.
Database terms: a table holds data about one kind of thing; a record is one row (one pupil); a field is one column (Surname); a key field (primary key) is unique for each record (Pupil ID).
Queries find records that match conditions (e.g. Class = 'Form 3' AND Mark > 15).

sections.heading: Presentation software
sections.text:
PowerPoint, LibreOffice Impress and Google Slides make slides for talks, lessons and meetings. You can add text, pictures, charts, video, animations and transitions.
Good slides use few words, big clear text, good contrast and relevant pictures. The speaker explains; the slides support.

sections.heading: Databases
sections.text:
A database stores large amounts of organised data so it can be searched, sorted and reported. Schools, hospitals and banks use them.
• A table holds data about one kind of thing (pupils).
• A record is one row: everything about one pupil.
• A field is one column: Surname, Class, Fee balance.
• The key field (primary key) is unique for each record, such as Pupil ID.

sections.heading: Queries and reports
sections.text:
A query asks the database for records that match conditions: Class = 'Form {3}' AND Fee balance > {0} finds Form {3} pupils who still owe fees.
Remember: > means 'greater than', so a mark equal to the limit is not included; >= includes it.
Reports present the results neatly for printing.

key_words.meaning: an organised collection of data that can be searched
one row of data about one item
a field unique for each record

mistake.wrong: A field is all the data about one pupil
mistake.right: That is a record; a field is one column
mistake.why: Records are rows; fields are columns.

worked_example.problem: A school database table holds pupils' ID, name, class and fee balance. Name the key field and explain why.
steps: Names can be repeated (two pupils called Ngozi).
The ID is different for every pupil.
So Pupil ID is the key field: it identifies each record uniquely.

cards.idea: Presentation software makes slides for talks.
A record is a row; a field is a column; the key field is unique.
A query finds the records that match conditions.

check.prompt: A table has these marks: {a}, {b}, {c}, {d}, {e}, {f}. A query selects records with Mark > {k}. How many records are found?

pick.q: Showing slides at a school science fair
Storing and searching the records of 1500 pupils
pick.y: Databases search and sort large data sets.

pick.q: Finding all pupils who still owe fees
In a database table of pupils, what is a record?
pick.r: all the data about one pupil (one row)
e: A database can have many tables.

pick.r: one category of data, such as Date of birth (a column)

pick.q: Why is Pupil ID used as the key field rather than Surname?
pick.r: IDs are unique; surnames can be repeated
w: IDs are always numbers less than 10
pick.y: A primary key identifies each record.

pick.q: Which is good advice for presentation slides?
pick.r: Use few words, large clear text and relevant pictures
w: Fill every slide with long paragraphs
Use tiny text to fit more
Add as many animations as possible
e: Audiences cannot read long paragraphs while listening.
Tiny text cannot be read from the back.
pick.y: Slides support the speaker; they do not replace the talk.

pick.r: the visual effect when moving from one slide to the next

pick.q: Why is a database better than a word-processed list for 1500 pupils' records?
pick.r: It can quickly search, sort and report on the data
e: That is not the main benefit.
